interpretation: Empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR is not a single semantic class. Workspace evidence establishes at least four distinct meanings across different rows: report-only monitoring (permit 'Report' cells and CSV AVG rows without numeric standard units), non-applicable mass-load statistical bases (Q1/N/A columns with numeric limits on sibling concentration rows), pass/fail WET reporting (pass=0;fail=1 unit encoding and comment), and geometric-mean aggregated reporting. The candidate label numeric_limit is not supported: no empty row carries a populated LIMIT_VALUE_STANDARD_UNITS comparison value, and permit text maps the corresponding cells to Report or N/A rather than a recoverable numeric effluent limit. No workspace source defines a uniform field-level rule that classifies all empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR rows for Purpose A comparison.
remaining_uncertainty: The obligation asks for one classification of empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR, but retained evidence shows heterogeneous semantics that depend on statistical base, DMR_COMMENT_TEXT, unit encoding, and permit-table context. All 57 empty rows share LIMIT_TYPE_CODE=ENF, which conflicts with a blanket report-only reading. Only 3 of 12 permit packages were opened; not every empty-limit row was matched to permit narrative. No ICIS/NPDES codebook in the workspace defines LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR emptiness. FY2025 DMR measurements contain zero rows with empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR, so Purpose A blocking is inferred from permit_limit structure rather than observed measurement joins.
